items.q: Commonest presentation of nasopharyngeal carcinoma is what?
o: Painless cervical lymph node mass (levels II and V)
items.exp: Rich submucosal lymphatics metastasise early (often bilaterally) while primary remains asymptomatic, so neck mass dominates presentations in endemic series. Posterior triangle level V nodes are classic.
r: Incorrect. Hoarseness is laryngeal.
Correct. Neck nodes present first.
Incorrect. Stridor is airway lesion.
Incorrect. Dental pain is maxillary disease.

items.q: Unilateral serous otitis media in a 50 year old from endemic region mandates what examination?
o: Nasopharyngeal endoscopy (with biopsy or imaging as found)
items.exp: Tumour at torus tubarius blocks tube causing effusion; inserting grommet without scoping misses NPC and can seed delay. Scope first, image and biopsy lesions.
r: Incorrect. Audiogram does not find cause.
Correct. Scope nasopharynx first.
Incorrect. Tube before scope is classic error.
Incorrect. Drops cannot reach cause.
items.kp: Adult one sided glue ear: scope before tube.

items.q: First cranial nerve typically affected by skull base NPC invasion causing diplopia is which?
items.exp: Long intracranial abducens course and Dorello canal vulnerability plus cavernous proximity make lateral gaze palsy earliest; lower cranial nerves follow jugular or hypoglossal canal extension later.
r: Incorrect. Vision falls with orbital apex late disease.
Correct. Abducens VI first commonly.
Incorrect. Facial nerve petrous route later.
Incorrect. XII is late skull base sign.
items.kp: Sixth nerve falls first to skull base cancer.

items.q: Plasma biomarker used in NPC screening and monitoring is what?
items.exp: Circulating EBV DNA mirrors tumour load, used in endemic population screening trials and post treatment surveillance for recurrence, alongside EBV serology (VCA IgA historical).
r: Incorrect. PSA is prostate.
Correct. Plasma EBV DNA tracks NPC.
Incorrect. CEA monitors colorectal.
Incorrect. CA19 9 is pancreaticobiliary.
items.kp: EBV in blood betrays nasopharynx cancer.

items.q: Primary curative treatment for most NPC is what and why?
o: Radiotherapy (with concurrent chemotherapy if advanced) due surgical inaccessibility and radiosensitivity
items.exp: Deep skull base location forbids clear surgical margins while tumour is radiosensitive; IMRT with concurrent cisplatin patterns for stage II onward improves survival, surgery salvages selected recurrences.
r: Incorrect. Anatomy prevents radical primary surgery.
Correct. Radiation based primary cure.
Incorrect. Chemo alone insufficient local cure.
Incorrect. Cancer progresses untreated.
items.kp: Beam reaches where knife cannot: NPC.

items.q: Trotter triad in NPC classically comprises which three?
o: Deafness, trigeminal pain, palatal immobility ipsilateral
items.exp: Historical triad from lateral wall invasion: Eustachian conductive deafness, V3 distribution pain and soft palate paralysis (levator involvement), taught as skull base spread pattern.
r: Correct. Deaf ear, jaw pain, palate still.
Incorrect. Those are ear neuroma features.
Incorrect. Symptoms occur but not triad.
Incorrect. Orbital invasion late differs.

items.q: Midline smooth nasopharyngeal cyst found incidentally on MRI in adult is most likely what?
items.exp: Thornwaldt cyst sits midline posterior nasopharynx between longus muscles, usually incidental, occasionally infected causing halitosis and postnasal discharge treated by marsupialisation. Lateral fossa masses worry for tumour instead.
r: Incorrect. Cancer favours lateral fossa asymmetry.
Correct. Midline Thornwaldt cyst benign.
Incorrect. Angiofibroma lateral vascular teen mass.
Incorrect. Encephalocele pulsatile with skull defect clues.
items.kp: Midline cyst is remnant, lateral mass is warning.

items.q: Regrown bulky adenoids in a 40 year old adult should prompt consideration of what besides chronic rhinitis?
items.exp: Adenoids involute after childhood; adult hypertrophy needs nasopharyngeal malignancy, lymphoma and immune suppression workup with biopsy, not assumption of allergy.
r: Incorrect. Adult regrowth is abnormal.
Correct. Exclude lymphoma and immune causes.
Incorrect. Ear bone disease unrelated.
Incorrect. Not physiological cause.

items.q: Endemic NPC strongest environmental and viral pairing is what?
o: EBV plus genetic susceptibility and salted fish nitrosamines (southern Chinese populations)
items.exp: Non keratinising endemic NPC integrates EBV latency with HLA genetics and early life nitrosamine diet; keratinising type in non endemic areas behaves more like other head neck squamous cancers.
r: Incorrect. HPV drives oropharyngeal tonsil cancer.
Correct. EBV, genes and salted fish.
Incorrect. Asbestos is mesothelial.
Incorrect. EBV defines endemic biology.
items.kp: Virus plus genes plus salted fish equals endemic NPC.

items.q: MRI is preferred over CT for NPC staging chiefly because it best shows what?
o: Skull base invasion, perineural spread, retropharyngeal nodes and intracranial extent
items.exp: Soft tissue contrast defines submucosal primary, foraminal and cavernous invasion and node levels for radiation fields; CT complements cortical bone and EBV DNA quantifies burden separately.
r: Incorrect. CT dental bone wins there.
Correct. Soft tissue and skull base spread.
Incorrect. Bone is CT advantage.
Incorrect. Blood test measures EBV.
items.kp: MRI maps soft invasion for the beam.
